clinicalPearls: SEMD is a heterogeneous family of skeletal dysplasias defined by combined radiographic involvement of the vertebrae (spondylo-), the epiphyses and the metaphyses.
It is separated from spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia (spine plus epiphyses) and spondylometaphyseal dysplasia (spine plus metaphyses) by the simultaneous epiphyseal and metaphyseal changes.
The Strudwick type is caused by COL2A1 (type II collagen) mutations and shows the characteristic dappled or mottled metaphyses.
Subtypes are increasingly gene-defined: MMP13 (Missouri type), ACAN (aggrecan type), DDR2 (short limb-hand/abnormal calcification type) and PAPSS2 (Pakistani type).
The joint-laxity forms are distinct: the leptodactylic type from KIF22 and the Beighton type from proteoglycan-linker gene B3GALT6.
Disproportionate short stature (often short-trunk), scoliosis, and progressive joint and hip problems are common across the group.
Odontoid hypoplasia and atlantoaxial instability may occur, particularly in the type II collagen forms — screen before anaesthesia or contact activity.
Diagnosis combines detailed radiographic phenotyping with targeted or panel-based genetic testing; inheritance varies by subtype (dominant, recessive or X-linked).
reference.pathophysiology: Spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia is not a single disease but a group unified by radiographic involvement of the spine, epiphyses and metaphyses, in which each subtype has a distinct molecular basis affecting cartilage matrix or growth-plate biology. The Strudwick type arises from dominant mutations in COL2A1, disturbing type II collagen and producing dappled metaphyses. The Missouri type is caused by mutations in MMP13 (matrix metalloproteinase-13) that impair collagen turnover at the growth plate. Other forms include the aggrecan type from ACAN; the short limb-hand type with abnormal calcification from DDR2 (a collagen-activated receptor tyrosine kinase); and the Pakistani type from PAPSS2, which is required for the sulphate activation that underpins proteoglycan sulphation. The joint-laxity subtypes include the leptodactylic type from KIF22 (a kinesin involved in chromosome segregation and chondrocyte function) and the Beighton type from B3GALT6, a glycosyltransferase in proteoglycan-linker biosynthesis. The shared theme is disruption of the cartilaginous growth plate and of epiphyseal and metaphyseal ossification, but the causative gene determines the precise phenotype, inheritance and recurrence risk.
additionalDifferentials: Spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia congenita and tarda (COL2A1; X-linked TRAPPC2) — spine and epiphyses without metaphyseal change
Spondylometaphyseal dysplasia, e.g., Kozlowski type (TRPV4) — spine and metaphyses without epiphyseal change
Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (COMP, MATN3, type IX collagen)
Achondrogenesis and hypochondrogenesis (COL2A1) at the severe end of the type II collagen spectrum
additionalInvestigations: Full skeletal survey including lateral spine and skull to characterise the spondylo-, epi- and metaphyseal features
Flexion-extension cervical spine imaging to assess odontoid hypoplasia and atlantoaxial instability
Molecular genetic testing by targeted gene, skeletal dysplasia panel or exome
Ophthalmology review for myopia and retinal detachment risk in type II collagen disorders
Serial growth monitoring with disproportion measurements (sitting height, arm span)
Audiology assessment where syndromic overlap is suspected
Family segregation studies and a detailed pedigree to define inheritance
redFlags: Signs of cervical myelopathy from atlantoaxial instability
Rapidly progressive scoliosis with respiratory compromise
Acute visual symptoms suggesting retinal detachment in type II collagen forms
Peri-anaesthetic risk from unrecognised cervical instability during airway management
reference.prognosis: The outlook is highly variable by subtype: many people achieve independent function with disproportionate short stature, while orthopaedic complications such as scoliosis, early joint degeneration and cervical instability drive morbidity. Life expectancy is usually normal in the common types.
pitfalls: Lumping all SEMD together and missing the specific gene diagnosis that guides prognosis and recurrence risk
Overlooking cervical instability before anaesthesia or before permitting contact activity
Missing ocular complications in the type II collagen (COL2A1) disorders
Confusing the dappled metaphyses of the Strudwick type with rickets or osteomyelitis
references: Nosology and classification of genetic skeletal disorders
management: No disease-specific pharmacotherapy; management is orthopaedic, functional and surveillance-based across the subtypes
Orthopaedic management of scoliosis, hip disease and joint problems, including bracing and joint-preserving or replacement surgery
Assess and stabilise cervical instability from odontoid hypoplasia and atlantoaxial laxity before anaesthesia or contact activity
Ophthalmology surveillance for myopia and retinal detachment in the type II collagen (COL2A1) subtypes
Serial growth monitoring with disproportion measurements, and physiotherapy to maintain mobility and joint function
Audiology assessment where syndromic overlap is suspected
Multidisciplinary clinical genetics and skeletal dysplasia care
Genetic counselling tailored to the inheritance of the specific gene-defined subtype
